newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says anthrax outbreak has ended.
newsitem.headline: Australia says anthrax outbreak has ended.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday the anthrax outbreak in the state of Victoria was officially over.
"I'm advised the chief veterinary officer for Victoria, based on sound scientific grounds and under accepted international guidelines, has declared the outbreak at an end," Anderson told reporters.
"While there has never been reason for concerns on the part of Australian consumers and trading partners, this announcement provides a further level of comfort," he said.
"It should further reassure those countries who have sought Australian assurances on anthrax."
But Anderson said the declaration did not mean that there would be no future incidents of anthrax in Australia, although all steps would be taken to mimimise its occurence.

"The proficient and swift handling of the outbreak by Australian industry and authorities should reinforce confidence among trading partners in this country's ability to handle similar incidents in such a way as to ensure the safety of exports of animals and animal products," he said.
Anthrax is a bacterial disease which causes rapid death in cattle and sheep, but which generally does not affect humans. It cannot be caught through consumption of processed diary products.
